questions.question: For the homogeneous equation $x_{t+k}+a_{k-1}x_{t+k-1}+\cdots+a_0x_t=0$ ($a_0\ne0$, constant coefficients) with characteristic polynomial $p(r)=r^k+a_{k-1}r^{k-1}+\cdots+a_0$, why is $x_t=r^t$ with $r\ne0$ a solution exactly when $p(r)=0$?
options: Substituting gives $p(r^t)=0$, which holds for $t=0$ only if $p(1)=0$.
Each root of $p$ is an equilibrium, and equilibria are solutions.

questions.question: For the homogeneous equation $x_{t+k}+a_{k-1}x_{t+k-1}+\cdots+a_0x_t=0$ ($a_0\ne0$, constant coefficients), why is $r=0$ never a root of the characteristic polynomial $p(r)=r^k+a_{k-1}r^{k-1}+\cdots+a_0$?
options: Because $0^t$ is undefined, so $r=0$ is excluded.
Because the leading coefficient of $p$ equals $1$.
Because characteristic roots must be positive reals.

questions.question: A homogeneous linear difference equation of order $3$ has constant real coefficients and $a_0\ne0$. How many characteristic roots does it have, counted with multiplicity?
options: Exactly $3$, some of which may be complex
Exactly $3$, all of them real numbers
At most $3$, and possibly none at all

questions.question: For a homogeneous linear difference equation with constant coefficients, let $r$ be a simple (multiplicity $1$) characteristic root. Is $x_t=t\,r^t$ then a solution?
options: Yes: multiplying a solution by $t$ always gives a solution.
No: $t\,r^t$ is never a solution of such an equation.
No: $t\,r^t$ solves only when $r$ has multiplicity at least $2$.

questions.question: A homogeneous linear difference equation with constant coefficients has the real characteristic root $r=-2$. What kind of solution does $x_t=(-2)^t$ describe?
options: A sequence that alternates in sign while its size doubles
A sequence that decreases steadily, halving each period
A sequence that decreases steadily, losing $2$ each period
No real solution, since a negative root needs complex numbers

questions.question: What is the characteristic polynomial $p(r)$ of the difference equation $x_{t+2}=5x_{t+1}-6x_t$, $t=0,1,2,\dots$?
Which geometric sequence solves $x_{t+2}-x_{t+1}-6x_t=0$, $t=0,1,2,\dots$?
The characteristic roots of $x_{t+3}-2x_{t+2}+5x_{t+1}-4x_t=0$, $t=0,1,2,\dots$, are $r_1,r_2,r_3$ (with multiplicity). By Vieta's formulas, what is the product $r_1r_2r_3$?
What is the equilibrium of the inhomogeneous equation $x_{t+2}-0.5\,x_{t+1}+0.25\,x_t=6$, $t=0,1,2,\dots$, using $x^*=b/p(1)$ with its characteristic polynomial $p$?
The equation $x_{t+2}-6x_{t+1}+9x_t=0$, $t=0,1,2,\dots$, has characteristic polynomial $p(r)=(r-3)^2$. Which sequence is a solution?
Consider $x_{t+2}-3x_{t+1}+2x_t=5$, $t=0,1,2,\dots$, with characteristic polynomial $p(r)=r^2-3r+2$. Which statement about its equilibria is correct?
options: $x^*=5/p(1)$ is undefined, so every constant is an equilibrium.
There is none, since $p(1)=0$ makes a constant give $0\ne5$.
$x^*=5$, since a constant solution must equal the right side.

questions.question: A homogeneous difference equation of order $3$ with real constant coefficients has the characteristic root $2+\mathrm{i}$. Which description of its other two roots is correct?
A homogeneous linear difference equation with constant coefficients has characteristic polynomial $p(r)=(r-2)(r-3)$. Which sequence is guaranteed to be a solution?
The equation $x_{t+2}-3x_{t+1}+2x_t=0$, $t=0,1,2,\dots$, has characteristic roots $1$ and $2$. Which sequence is the solution with $x_0=3$ and $x_1=5$?

Because $r^2+1$ has the nonreal roots $\pm\mathrm{i}=\mathrm{e}^{\pm\mathrm{i}\pi/2}$, real solutions of $x_{t+2}+x_t=0$ can be written with cosines and sines. Starting from $x_0=1$, $x_1=0$, which formula gives $x_t$?
A homogeneous equation $x_{t+2}+a_1x_{t+1}+a_0x_t=0$, $t=0,1,2,\dots$, with constant coefficients has characteristic roots $3$ and $-1$. Which equation is it?
For $x_{t+2}-4x_{t+1}+4x_t=0$, $t=0,1,2,\dots$, with the double characteristic root $2$, why are the sequences $c\cdot2^t$ alone not enough to describe all solutions?
options: $2^t$ does not solve it, since a double root yields no geometric solution.
Its solutions are not closed under addition, as $p$ has a repeated factor.
Each solution needs three initial values, as the root counts twice.

questions.question: A real homogeneous equation has the nonreal characteristic roots $r=\rho \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\theta}$ and $\bar r=\rho \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}\theta}$. Why is the real sequence $x_t=\rho^t\cos(\theta t)$ a solution?
options: It equals $(\operatorname{Re}r)^t$, the real part raised to the power $t$.
It equals $\tfrac{1}{2}(r^t+\bar r^{\,t})$, a combination of two solutions.
It is periodic, and periodic sequences solve such equations.
It equals $\rho^t$, since $\cos(\theta t)$ is a bounded factor.

questions.question: The equation $x_{t+2}+x_{t+1}+x_t=0$, $t=0,1,2,\dots$, has characteristic polynomial $r^2+r+1$. What is the smallest period shared by all of its real solutions (the least $T\ge1$ with $x_{t+T}=x_t$ for all $t$)?
options: No period: nonreal roots give no periodic solutions

questions.question: For $x_{t+2}-5x_{t+1}+6x_t=4$, $t=0,1,2,\dots$, with characteristic polynomial $(r-2)(r-3)$, which sequence is the solution with $x_0=3$ and $x_1=4$?
